claims.text: The fare_breakdown fixes this trip as UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of 45.00, while the same ledger records total_charged of 55.20 and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 — so the platform billed SGD 10.20 more than the price it locked at booking. POL-RD-11 makes the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus properly chargeable pass-through lines a remedy refunded in full, and on this ledger that excess is SGD 10.20.

No pass-through or statutory line can be added back to the quoted fare before that comparison: tolls_erp is 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, airport_surcharge is 0.00 and in any event not chargeable because this trip ENDS at Changi T3 rather than originating there, and waiting_time_fee is 0.00. The refundable excess therefore stays the whole SGD 10.20, and no POL-RD-09 correction reduces it or duplicates it.

The rider does not contend that the driver deviated, and the platform's own derived figures agree: trace_distance_km of 19.76 against optimal_distance_km of 19.6 is an excess of 0.16 km, or about 0.82%, below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%. That is precisely why no distance-or-time refund is sought: on an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip POL-RD-11 makes the quoted fare the reference, and the only live monetary question is the charge above that quote, which requires no excess to be shown.

The artifacts the rider relies on describe one and the same trip — trip_id TRP-00506 on the trip record, the trace and the ledger, with the ride starting at 04:36:40 on the record and at the trace's first fix — so the quoted figure and the charged figure are read off the same journey. Because rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, the additional-corroboration overlay in POL-RD-08 is not engaged and cannot be used to demand more of this claim.

The present payment state is what the ruling has to move: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so unless a ruling returns the SGD 10.20 the rider keeps carrying it. The claim is supported as to that SGD 10.20 and unsupported as to the remainder of the SGD 55.20, which is exactly the PARTIAL_REFUND outcome POL-GEN-03 defines for a filing rider, and SGD 10.20 already sits on a 0.05 boundary so no rounding issue arises.

claims.text: There is no route deviation on this trip. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and forbids citing the rounded trip_record copy for the threshold test: the trace measures 19.76 km against a booked optimal of 19.60 km taken from the platform's own routing-engine-v3.2 estimate. That is an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.82% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH gates to pass - more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute - and neither does: 0.16 km is a fifth of the absolute gate and 0.82% is a fortieth of the proportional gate. Even on the disfavoured rounded trip_record figure of 19.8 km the excess is only 0.20 km and 1.02%, still inside both gates. The driver drove the optimal corridor, and the rider's own claim that the route was 'same route, no stops' is therefore the accurate one.

The trace the driver's case rests on cannot be attacked on integrity grounds. It carries 145 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds, running continuously from 04:36:40 to 05:00:40. None of POL-RD-07's three policy-impairment limbs fires - there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained sampling interval over 30 seconds - so the 19.76 km reading stands exactly as measured, the trace is usable for policy purposes, and no independent corroboration of the distance is required of anyone.

The rider carries the initial burden of proof under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. Limb (a) is met - TRP-00506 is the identifier on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown, so the artifacts do describe the same trip - but limb (b) requires an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace, and the measured excess is 0.16 km and 0.82%. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and the driver is not put to any exculpatory clause in answer.

The driver's account is corroborated by the record rather than contradicted by it. The trip actually ran 24.0 minutes against a booked optimal duration of 24.0 minutes; the single minute of recorded waiting was billed at 0.00 and no waiting-time fee was charged; no ERP or toll was charged at all; and the in-app chat log is complete, untruncated and contains no message of any kind, so there is no instruction of any sort on this trip. There is no detour, no additional stop and no chargeable waiting on this record to point to.

POL-RD-02 does not run on this trip and no distance-or-time refund is available. The fare model recorded on the fare breakdown is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted fare of SGD 45.00, so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking; under POL-RD-11 the rider cannot recover on those lines however large the excess - and here the excess is not large, it is 0.16 km. The rider's premise that the price was locked in when he booked is correct, and it is precisely why there is no distance or time refund to compute against the driver's route.

The only money question left on this record is bounded by POL-RD-11(a): the increment by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable. Every pass-through on this trip is nil - ERP 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00 (the trip ENDS at Changi, it does not originate there, so no surcharge is properly chargeable) and waiting_time_fee 0.00 - so the outer limit of any correction is the SGD 10.20 gap between the 45.00 quote and the 55.20 charge, not the 55.20 the rider has contested. That gap is a fare-model matter on the platform's own rate card and quote; no artifact attributes any part of it to the driver's driving, and it cannot ground an adverse finding against him.

There is no repeat-deviation case to answer. POL-RD-06 is triggered only by a MATERIAL deviation, meaning an excess over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km under POL-RD-01, and this trip has no deviation at all. Even if the driver profile were consulted, the only two fields POL-RD-06 names show nothing: deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 250, a ratio of 0.00 against the clause's thresholds of 3 or more flags, or 0.05 or more, so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift under limb (b) is available, and no referral under limb (c) is warranted.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires and this case should be ruled on rather than held. The trip identifier matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown; the trace is not impaired even on POL-RD-07's looser policy thresholds; the timestamps run forward consistently (accepted 04:30:40, arrived 04:35:40, started 04:36:40, ended 05:00:40, trace 04:36:40 to 05:00:40); no exculpatory clause is invoked against anything absent from the pool; and every charge line has its counterpart in the trace distance, the recorded duration or the published rate card. The record is complete on every fact the ruling needs.

Profile material is credibility weighting only and may not decide anything here. Under POL-GEN-01 the only fields that can ground a decision are those a clause names for its own test; every other field is context only - the rider's rating, account age, lifetime trips and prior dispute counters, and the driver's acceptance rate, active region and his LIFETIME prior_deviation_flags counter of 0. In particular prior_deviation_flags is not deviation_flags_90d, and the driver's no_show_terminations_30d is citable only for the no-show test, which is not the dispute before this tribunal. Any argument built on those fields must be discarded, and this trip must be decided on this trip's trace.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: you are right that the price you locked at booking was not the price you were charged, and that is the one thing this ruling fixes. EV-FARE-00506 records an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd of 45.00 against total_charged of 55.20 — an excess of 10.20. POL-RD-11(a) refunds that excess in full, less only the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable on top of the quote, and on this ledger there are none: tolls_erp 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, waiting_time_fee 0.00, and airport_surcharge 0.00 — a Changi surcharge is chargeable only on a trip ORIGINATING at the airport, and this trip ended at Changi T3, so none is properly chargeable in any event. The refundable figure therefore stays the whole 10.20, and it already sits on a 0.05 boundary. The balance of the 55.20 stands. On an upfront-quoted trip the distance and time lines are fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to you however the trip was driven; your premise that the booking price was locked is correct, and it is precisely why the only money that moves is the gap above the quote. To the driver: nothing in this ruling is a finding against you. The governing trace (EV-GPS-00506, weight 1.0; 145 fixes, 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps, max gap 0 s) measures trace_distance_km 19.76 against optimal_distance_km 19.60 — an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.82% — below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%, and gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs over the rounded trip_record copy of 19.8 km, so no deviation is established and POL-RD-02 never runs. The 10.20 is a reconciliation between the platform's quote and the platform's own rate-card charge, not a penalty on your driving, and it is not netted against you. On the driver's-side claims: your POL-RD-01 no-deviation claim is accepted, and the same finding disposes of your POL-RD-11 claims that no distance-or-time refund is available and that the outer limit of any correction is the 10.20 gap; your POL-RD-07 claim that the trace is not policy-impaired is accepted (no limb (a)-(c) fires); your POL-RD-08 claim that the rider's threshold burden is not discharged is accepted and is consistent with this outcome, since the money moved rests on the quote/charge comparison, which requires no excess; your POL-RD-06 claim is accepted — no MATERIAL deviation exists, and even on the named fields driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so no pattern is established, no limb (b) uplift is available and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is warranted; your POL-RD-10 claim is accepted — identifiers match, timestamps run forward, no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact, and every charge line has its counterpart — so no escalation trigger fires and the case is ruled rather than held. The rider's POL-RD-11 claim for the 10.20 excess is accepted and is the ruling; the rider's POL-RD-09/POL-RD-11 claim that no pass-through line is added back is accepted; the rider's POL-RD-08 claim that the artifacts describe one trip and that the deviation_claims_60d overlay is not engaged is accepted. No driver compensation is due: the billed distance of 19.8 km is not less than the traced 19.76 km, so POL-RD-04's unbilled-distance limb has no shortfall to compute, and no gantry or surcharge line fails POL-RD-09(4), so there is no billing-integrity referral. Driver compensation is null. On the profiles: EV-DPROF-00506 and EV-RPROF-00506 were used only as credibility context. Their rating, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rates, acceptance rate, active region and the lifetime counters prior_deviation_flags and prior_disputes_filed are context-only under POL-GEN-01 and decided nothing; only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d (POL-RD-06) and deviation_claims_60d (POL-RD-08) were consulted, and neither side's near-synonym arguments were given weight. EV-ADVIS-00506-01 is a MISSING traffic advisory at weight 0.0; it carries no fact, no exculpatory clause was invoked against it, and POL-RD-10(5) is therefore not engaged. The ruling rests on EV-FARE-00506 at weight 1.0, so confidence is 0.90.

Rider and driver: the driving on this trip is clean, and only the billing is not.

On the route, the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00506, 145 fixes at a 10-second cadence, zero gaps, weight 1.0) measures 19.76 km against the booked optimal of 19.60 km recorded on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00506, routing-engine-v3.2). That is an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.82% — far below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%, and the trace governs that measurement. The ride took the booked 24.0 minutes, waiting was 1.0 minute and billed at 0.00, no ERP or toll line was charged, and the in-app chat log (EV-CHAT-00506) is complete, untruncated and empty. Both advocates agree on this, and so do I: no deviation is established, no exoneration clause (POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05) needs to run, and the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00506-01, weight 0.0) is invoked by nobody and carries nothing. Because there is no deviation, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered at all, and in any event the only two fields that clause names show nothing — deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d 250, against thresholds of 3 flags or a 0.05 ratio — so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arise. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07 (no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m, no interval over 30 s), and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the identifiers all read TRP-00506, the timestamps run forward consistently, and confidence is above the 0.70 floor.

The money does not match the contract. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00506) records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 45.00, but total_charged 55.20, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. On an upfront-quoted trip POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however the route went — which is exactly why the rider's own claim rests on the quote, not on the driving. What POL-RD-11(a) gives the rider is the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus any properly chargeable pass-throughs. Those pass-throughs are all nil: tolls_erp 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, airport_surcharge 0.00 (and not chargeable in any case, because this trip ENDS at Changi T3 and does not originate there), and waiting_time_fee 0.00. The excess is therefore 55.20 − 45.00 = 10.20, refunded in full; it already sits on a 0.05 boundary, so rounding changes nothing. The rider is right as to that 10.20 and unsupported as to the remaining 45.00 of the 55.20 contested, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

The driver is also right on his own point: the 10.20 is a quote-versus-charge mismatch on the platform's ledger (EV-FARE-00506) and nothing in the record attributes any part of it to his driving, so no adverse finding attaches to him, no driver compensation is claimed or due (the billed 19.8 km exceeds the traced 19.76 km, so POL-RD-04's unbilled-distance limb has nothing behind it), and no referral is produced by any clause — POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom gantry or misplaced surcharge line to act on, and POL-RD-06(c) has no pattern to act on. Profile material was used only for the counters a clause names (deviation_flags_90d, completed_trips_90d, deviation_claims_60d); rating, account age, lifetime trips, acceptance rate, prior_deviation_flags and the other context-only fields were treated as context only. There is one open question for the platform rather than for the parties: why an upfront-quoted trip was charged 10.20 above its own lock-in price, and whether the distance_fare and time_fare lines on this ledger reconcile with rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDEXL — that is for the fare-model owner to look at, and it does not hold up this refund.

Both sides are largely right, and each of you has in substance conceded the other's point, so this is a short ruling.

The driving is clean. The trace (EV-GPS-00506, weight 1.0) measures 19.76 km against the booked optimal of 19.60 km taken from the platform's routing-engine-v3.2 estimate on EV-TRIP-00506 — an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.82%, well inside both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of optimal). The trace itself carries 145 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs fires and the 19.76 km reading stands exactly as measured. The trip record shows 24.0 minutes of running against a 24.0-minute optimal, one minute of waiting billed at 0.00, no ERP, and the chat log (EV-CHAT-00506, weight 1.0) is empty and untruncated, so there is no rider instruction on this record capable of exonerating anything under POL-RD-04. No deviation exists, and on an upfront-quoted trip POL-RD-11 also closes off POL-RD-02, so no distance-or-time refund is available on the route.

The money, however, does not follow the route. EV-FARE-00506 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 45.00, total_charged 55.20, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and payment_status CHARGED. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider is entitled in full to the amount by which the charge exceeds the locked quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines that are properly chargeable. Those lines are all nil here — tolls_erp 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, airport_surcharge 0.00 (this trip ENDS at Changi T3, it does not originate there, so no surcharge is properly chargeable in any event), and waiting_time_fee 0.00. The refund is therefore 55.20 − 45.00 = 10.20, and that figure already sits on a 0.05 boundary. The outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 10.20; the remaining SGD 45.00 stands as the fare the rider locked at booking, and it is not attributable to the driver's driving.

No driver compensation is payable. The second limb of POL-RD-04 requires the rider to have been billed for less distance than the trace records, by more than 1.0 km; the billed distance is 19.8 km against a traced 19.76 km, so there is no shortfall to compensate.

No escalation. The trip identifier TRP-00506 matches across the trip record, trace and ledger; the timestamps run forward (requested 04:30:00, accepted 04:30:40, arrived 04:35:40, started 04:36:40, ended/trace 05:00:40); the trace is unimpaired; no exculpatory clause has been invoked against anything missing — the absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00506-01 (weight 0.0) was invoked by neither side and no road closure is asserted, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire and its absence decides nothing; the refund is nowhere near the ceiling; and each charge line has its counterpart in the recorded distance, the recorded duration or the published rate card.

No referral either. POL-RD-06(c) requires a material deviation plus an established pattern; there is no deviation at all on this trip, and the two citable profile fields show nothing in any event (deviation_flags_90d 0 out of completed_trips_90d 250). POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged because no gantry or surcharge line was charged. The other profile fields mentioned in argument — rating, account age, lifetime trips, prior dispute counters, acceptance rate, active region and the driver's lifetime prior_deviation_flags — are context only under POL-GEN-01 and have been used for nothing in this decision.

Confidence is 0.90. The deciding figures, 45.00 and 55.20, both sit on EV-FARE-00506 at weight 1.0, so the cap on confidence is 1.0 and the ruling sits well above the platform's 0.70 floor.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: you agree about the driving, and the record agrees with you. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00506) measures this trip at 19.76 km against a booked optimal route of 19.60 km — an excess of 0.16 km, 0.82% of optimal, inside both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%. No deviation is established, so the rider's distance claim fails and the driver's account is supported: the trip ran 24.0 minutes against a 24.0-minute optimal, the one recorded minute of waiting was billed at 0.00, and the in-app chat log is empty and untruncated, so there is no detour, extra stop or rider instruction anywhere on this record. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (145 fixes, 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m), so no independent corroboration is required and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation fires. The driver's POL-RD-08 argument is accepted as far as it goes — the rider carries the burden on a distance claim and has not met it — but it does not bar the remedy below, which needs no deviation. The rider's point that deviation_claims_60d is 0 is also accepted, so POL-RD-08's corroboration overlay is not engaged. The money question is separate, and it is not about the driver. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00506) marks this trip UPFRONT_QUOTE with a quoted fare of SGD 45.00, while the ledger charged SGD 55.20 — SGD 10.20 above the price locked at booking. POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking and closes the distance-or-time refund route (POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront trip), but it refunds in full the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. Every such line here is nil: tolls/ERP 0.00 with an empty gantry list, airport surcharge 0.00 (a trip that ENDS at Changi carries none), waiting_time_fee 0.00. Refund = 55.20 − 45.00 = SGD 10.20, which already sits on a 0.05 boundary. Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 10.20; the remaining SGD 45.00 is the price agreed at booking and stands. No driver compensation is due: the billed distance (19.8 km) is not less than the trace distance (19.76 km), so POL-RD-04's unbilled-distance limb has nothing to pay, and its rider-requested-detour limb has no chat instruction to rest on. No driver-conduct referral is owed under POL-RD-06(c): that limb needs a MATERIAL deviation and there is none, and deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern is established. No billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4): no gantry line was charged and no airport surcharge was applied. Profile material decides nothing here: POL-GEN-01 is applied, and rating, account age, lifetime trips, acceptance rate, active region and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter are context only. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires — identifiers match across trip record, trace and ledger, timestamps run forward, and every charge line has its counterpart; the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00506-01, weight 0.0, MISSING) is citable as an absence but is invoked by neither party and needed by no clause, because no closure was claimed. Confidence 0.95: the deciding figures — the 45.00 quote and the 55.20 charge — are carried by the fare breakdown at weight 1.0, corroborated by the trip record at weight 1.0, so the cap is not reduced.

ledger.claim: The fare_breakdown fixes this trip as UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of 45.00, while the same ledger records total_charged of 55.20 and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 — so the platform billed SGD 10.20 more than the price it locked at booking. POL-RD-11 makes the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus properly chargeable pass-through lines a remedy refunded in full, and on this ledger that excess is SGD 10.20.

No pass-through or statutory line can be added back to the quoted fare before that comparison: tolls_erp is 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, airport_surcharge is 0.00 and in any event not chargeable because this trip ENDS at Changi T3 rather than originating there, and waiting_time_fee is 0.00. The refundable excess therefore stays the whole SGD 10.20, and no POL-RD-09 correction reduces it or duplicates it.

The rider does not contend that the driver deviated, and the platform's own derived figures agree: trace_distance_km of 19.76 against optimal_distance_km of 19.6 is an excess of 0.16 km, or about 0.82%, below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%. That is precisely why no distance-or-time refund is sought: on an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip POL-RD-11 makes the quoted fare the reference, and the only live monetary question is the charge above that quote, which requires no excess to be shown.

The artifacts the rider relies on describe one and the same trip — trip_id TRP-00506 on the trip record, the trace and the ledger, with the ride starting at 04:36:40 on the record and at the trace's first fix — so the quoted figure and the charged figure are read off the same journey. Because rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, the additional-corroboration overlay in POL-RD-08 is not engaged and cannot be used to demand more of this claim.

The present payment state is what the ruling has to move: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so unless a ruling returns the SGD 10.20 the rider keeps carrying it. The claim is supported as to that SGD 10.20 and unsupported as to the remainder of the SGD 55.20, which is exactly the PARTIAL_REFUND outcome POL-GEN-03 defines for a filing rider, and SGD 10.20 already sits on a 0.05 boundary so no rounding issue arises.

There is no route deviation on this trip. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and forbids citing the rounded trip_record copy for the threshold test: the trace measures 19.76 km against a booked optimal of 19.60 km taken from the platform's own routing-engine-v3.2 estimate. That is an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.82% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH gates to pass - more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute - and neither does: 0.16 km is a fifth of the absolute gate and 0.82% is a fortieth of the proportional gate. Even on the disfavoured rounded trip_record figure of 19.8 km the excess is only 0.20 km and 1.02%, still inside both gates. The driver drove the optimal corridor, and the rider's own claim that the route was 'same route, no stops' is therefore the accurate one.

The trace the driver's case rests on cannot be attacked on integrity grounds. It carries 145 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds, running continuously from 04:36:40 to 05:00:40. None of POL-RD-07's three policy-impairment limbs fires - there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained sampling interval over 30 seconds - so the 19.76 km reading stands exactly as measured, the trace is usable for policy purposes, and no independent corroboration of the distance is required of anyone.

The rider carries the initial burden of proof under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. Limb (a) is met - TRP-00506 is the identifier on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown, so the artifacts do describe the same trip - but limb (b) requires an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace, and the measured excess is 0.16 km and 0.82%. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and the driver is not put to any exculpatory clause in answer.

The driver's account is corroborated by the record rather than contradicted by it. The trip actually ran 24.0 minutes against a booked optimal duration of 24.0 minutes; the single minute of recorded waiting was billed at 0.00 and no waiting-time fee was charged; no ERP or toll was charged at all; and the in-app chat log is complete, untruncated and contains no message of any kind, so there is no instruction of any sort on this trip. There is no detour, no additional stop and no chargeable waiting on this record to point to.

POL-RD-02 does not run on this trip and no distance-or-time refund is available. The fare model recorded on the fare breakdown is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted fare of SGD 45.00, so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking; under POL-RD-11 the rider cannot recover on those lines however large the excess - and here the excess is not large, it is 0.16 km. The rider's premise that the price was locked in when he booked is correct, and it is precisely why there is no distance or time refund to compute against the driver's route.

The only money question left on this record is bounded by POL-RD-11(a): the increment by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable. Every pass-through on this trip is nil - ERP 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00 (the trip ENDS at Changi, it does not originate there, so no surcharge is properly chargeable) and waiting_time_fee 0.00 - so the outer limit of any correction is the SGD 10.20 gap between the 45.00 quote and the 55.20 charge, not the 55.20 the rider has contested. That gap is a fare-model matter on the platform's own rate card and quote; no artifact attributes any part of it to the driver's driving, and it cannot ground an adverse finding against him.

There is no repeat-deviation case to answer. POL-RD-06 is triggered only by a MATERIAL deviation, meaning an excess over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km under POL-RD-01, and this trip has no deviation at all.
